explain.say: Jean Rhys read Jane Eyre and kept wondering about the woman locked in the attic, Bertha. In 1966, in her seventies, she published her answer: Wide Sargasso Sea, the story of Bertha's life before Thornfield, when she was Antoinette Cosway, a young Creole heiress in the Caribbean. A gentle note: it deals with slavery's aftermath, racism and madness.

explain.say: Look at the map. Antoinette grows up in Jamaica in the 1830s, just after slavery was abolished in the British Empire. Her family were enslavers, now ruined; their formerly enslaved neighbours resent them, and English people look down on them as Creoles. Where does Antoinette belong? Then marriage takes her across the Atlantic.

draw.label: Antoinette’s journey: Jamaica, a honeymoon on a smaller island, then an English attic

explain.say: The middle part is told by her husband, an unnamed Englishman we recognise as Rochester, who married her for her money. Letters from a man claiming to be her half-brother poison him against her. He starts calling her Bertha, a name she hates. Why is renaming someone such a powerful act?

explain.say: This is called writing back: a writer from a colonised place retells a classic from the side of the people it silenced. On the left, Brontë's Bertha, seen only through Jane and mad by inheritance. On the right, Rhys's Antoinette, who speaks, and whose madness grows from loss, racism and a cruel marriage. Does Rhys change how you read Jane Eyre?

In the last part Antoinette is locked in an English attic, guarded by Grace Poole. She dreams of setting the house on fire, then wakes, takes a candle, and walks out into the dark passage. We know how Jane Eyre ends. Wonderful work. Challenge: choose a minor character from a book you love and write one page in their voice.

faq.q: How is Wide Sargasso Sea connected to Jane Eyre?
faq.a: It is a prequel and reply to Jane Eyre, telling the early life of Bertha Mason, Rochester's first wife, from her own point of view, and ending just before the fire at Thornfield.
asks: Is Wide Sargasso Sea a prequel?

faq.q: Why does Rochester call Antoinette Bertha?
faq.a: As he turns against her, he renames her Bertha, taking away her identity and making her into the English wife he wants to control. Antoinette feels the new name is a kind of obeah, a spell to make her someone else.
A postcolonial practice of rewriting canonical European texts from the viewpoint of colonised or silenced characters. The term was popularised by the 1989 study The Empire Writes Back.

faq.q: How does Wide Sargasso Sea end?
faq.a: Locked in the attic at Thornfield, Antoinette dreams of burning the house, then wakes, takes a candle and goes out into the passage, leaving the ending of Jane Eyre to follow.

faq.q: What does Creole mean in Wide Sargasso Sea?
faq.a: Here it means a white person of European descent born in the Caribbean. Antoinette is mocked as a white cockroach by Black islanders and seen as not truly English by the English.
